title: SkipSR: Faster Super-Resolution with Token Skipping
claim: Standard models process every region uniformly; ours processes only the regions that need refinement, saving computation without quality loss.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, same photo with patch-grid overlays
description: Three side-by-side panels show the same beach scene, a white umbrella over a lounge chair, a turquoise sea and sand, under black-bordered captions. The left panel, 'Original Image', is the plain photo. The middle panel, 'Standard Diffusion Transformer', overlays a dense white grid of small rectangular patches across the whole image, which shows that every patch is processed. The right panel, 'SkipSR (Ours)', uses the same grid but only over the umbrella, the chair, the shoreline and the sand. The smooth sky and parts of the sea have no grid lines, so those patches are skipped. The eye goes first to the contrast between the full grid in the middle and the sparse grid on the right. There are no arrows, only captions.
caption: Patch Skipping.Standard diffusion SR models refine the entire input, while SkipSR identifies and upscales only the patches that need refinement. This significantly reduces computation with no loss in perceptual quality.
abstract: Diffusion-based super-resolution (SR) is a key component in video generation and video restoration, but is slow and expensive, limiting scalability to higher resolutions and longer videos. Our key insight is that many regions in video are inherently low-detail and gain little from refinement, yet current methods process all pixels uniformly. To take advantage of this, we propose SkipSR, a simple framework for accelerating video SR by identifying low-detail regions directly from low-resolution input, then skipping computation on them entirely, only super-resolving the areas that require refinement. This simple yet effective strategy preserves perceptual quality in both standard and one-step diffusion SR models while significantly reducing computation. In standard SR benchmarks, our method achieves up to 60% faster end-to-end latency than prior models on 720p videos with no perceptible loss in quality. Video demos are available at https://rccchoudhury.github.io/skipsr/
